chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him, “What is the muḥṣan, may Allah have mercy on you?” He said, “Whoever has a private-partner to whom he goes in the morning and returns in the evening, then he is a muḥṣan.”

key_terms.الْمُحْصَنُ: A legally protected married person subject to the ruling of iḥṣān
key_terms.فَرْجٌ: A lawful sexual partner or conjugal access in this legal context
key_terms.يَغْدُو عَلَيْهِ وَ يَرُوحُ: An expression indicating regular and ongoing access

ai.seo_question: Who is considered muḥṣan in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh definition of who is considered muḥṣan in the legal sense. It indicates that a person is muḥṣan when he has ongoing access to a lawful spouse, which is relevant to the legal rulings of zinā.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5022 - Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Ismail ibn Jabir, who reports by Abu Abdullah (as).

I asked Imam (as): "May Allah (swt) have mercy on you, who is considered Muhsan?"
Imam (as) replied: "Whoever has lawful access to a spouse in the morning and evening, he is Muhsan."
